summary_en: This single-arm Phase II trial tests whether leaving out radiation after surgery is possible and safe for selected people with HPV-associated oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma. Participants have transoral robotic surgery and no postoperative radiation, with routine clinical follow-up and serial ctHPVDNA testing (NavDx); how long and how often are not stated. The record says the study measures feasibility and oncologic safety of omitting radiation.
summary_es: Este ensayo de fase II con un solo grupo evalúa si es posible y seguro omitir la radioterapia después de la cirugía en personas seleccionadas con carcinoma de células escamosas de orofaringe asociado al VPH. Los participantes se someten a cirugía robótica transoral y no reciben radioterapia posoperatoria, con seguimiento clínico de rutina y pruebas seriadas de ADN tumoral del VPH en sangre (NavDx); la duración y la frecuencia no se indican. El registro indica que el estudio mide la viabilidad y la seguridad oncológica de omitir la radioterapia.
who_for: Biopsy-proven squamous cell carcinoma, p16 positive, and NavDx positive for HPV16 TTMV only.
Staged cT0-2 N1 M0 (AJCC 8th edition) with limited lymph node size and number.
Well lateralized tonsil, base of tongue, or glossotonsillar sulcus primary tumor.
10 or fewer pack-years of smoking, or no smoking for at least 5 years.
Suitable for transoral robotic surgery and platinum chemotherapy, with ECOG 0-1 and adequate blood, kidney and liver function.
not_for: Prior head and neck surgery or radiation that could change the meaning of pathology results.
Current immunosuppressive or disease-modifying rheumatoid drugs, or active lupus, scleroderma, or psoriatic arthritis.
Other cancer within 5 years (with listed exceptions), severe recent comorbidity, pregnancy or breastfeeding, or involuntary incarceration.
